newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cargo Sprinter to up Deutsche Bahn air cargo.
newsitem.headline: Cargo Sprinter to up Deutsche Bahn air cargo.

text.p: Deutsche Bahn AG said it aims to win back lost freight market share from road transport and move into the air cargo feeder market with its new Cargo Sprinter train.

DB Cargo rail freight divisional director, Eberhard Sinnecker, said at a Cargo Sprinter presentation on Wednesday that the train would save DB time and money through rapid coupling and offer clients a better service.
The Cargo Sprinter prototype with two drive units, three central wagons would be tested for a year before seven units go into regular service next autumn, he said.
Sinnecker told Reuters he wanted to target the land transport market for car parts, foodstuffs and industrial goods.
"We are going into market segments which are difficult to reach. We will start with containers because it is the fastest-growing market," he said.
It was too early to set a price but DB would charge market-orientated rates similar to those of trucking companies, he added.
Sinnecker said: "Air cargo is an area we are interested in. If there are routes with regular volumes, that would be interesting for us."
He said DB was looking at routes from Frankfurt to Zurich and Milan in particular.

Roland Heinisch, DB board member for rolling stock, said a new automatic train coupling and sharing system meant up to seven Cargo Sprinters could be connected into a single train up to 10 times more quickly than with conventional shunting.
The 91-metre train could operate at up to 100km/h carrying 160 tonnes of cargo in up to 10 containers or at 120km/h with 112 tonnes, he added.
Heinz Loerfing, board member of Cargo Sprinter manufacturer Windhoff AG, told Reuters the prototype had been built at a cost of 2.5 million marks.
DB Cargo spokesman Michael Adam said DB had paid a much lower price than this for the train but declined to disclose the exact sum. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
